answer: Sybil resistance here is a delayed, slashable bond tied to one signing key. A newcomer must lock spendable stake for several epochs before its grades or votes carry full weight. Until that seasoning completes, the bond is marked umber — unproven and cheap to abandon — and the agent may wander the ledger attesting work but cannot swing settlement. If clustering later shows one operator spinning many keys, the first bond is treated as a relic of a discarded identity and is burned, so farming extra accounts costs more than honest mining.
